auxiliary_material: The authors demonstrate the biological relevance of inosine quantification by showing that converting adenosine to inosine within the tumor microenvironment (TME) reverses immunosuppression. Mechanistically, increased inosine correlated with enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration, a shift from M2 to M1 macrophage phenotypes, and upregulation of cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-12p70). The study also validates that inosine can serve as an alternative carbon source for T cells under glucose-depleted conditions, supporting the rationale for monitoring these metabolites in cancer contexts.
outline_action: Use the reported LC-MS/MS parameters and SPME extraction technique as a preclinical example of technical feasibility for inosine quantification in solid tumors. Cite the observed murine baseline concentrations to illustrate typical orders of magnitude in tumor tissue, while explicitly distinguishing these from human reference ranges. Leverage the mechanistic findings (adenosine-to-inosine conversion effects on immunity) to justify the need for standardized human quantification protocols in the review, but note that the specific success criteria for human consensus and reference ranges remain unfulfilled by this source.
remaining_gap: The supplied material does not provide standardized analytical protocols for human serum or tumor tissue, as all quantification was performed in murine models (MC38 colorectal cancer). There are no human-specific reference concentration ranges for inosine or short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in cancer patients or healthy controls. Furthermore, the paper does not address SCFA quantification methods at all, nor does it cite or establish any consensus guidelines for clinical metabolite monitoring.
useful_material: This study details a specific LC-MS/MS method for quantifying inosine and adenosine in tumor tissue, utilizing an Agilent 1290 Infinity II UHPLC coupled to a 6475 Triple Quad mass spectrometer in positive MRM mode. Key parameters include a ZORBAX RRHD Eclipse Plus C18 column (150 mm × 3 mm, 1.8 µm), a water (0.1% formic acid)/acetonitrile gradient at 300 µL/min, and specific parent/product ion pairs for inosine (269.1/136.8) and adenosine (268.1/135.9). Sample processing employed hydrophilic-lipophilic balanced solid-phase microextraction (HLB-SPME) fibers inserted directly into murine tumors, with lamivudine as an internal standard. The authors reported a baseline adenosine concentration of approximately 0.04 µM in control mouse tumor tissue.
